Let \(X=\frac{A+C}{2}\) and \(Y=\frac{C-A}{2}\). Using \(h=b\sin C\) and the law of sines:
\[
\sin C-\sin A=\sin B\sin C.
\]
Since \(\sin B=\sin(A+C)\), we get
\[
2\cos X\sin Y=2\sin X\cos X\sin C,
\]
so
\[
\sin Y=\sin X\sin C.
\]
Thus the target expression is
\[
\sin Y+\cos X=\cos X+\sin X\sin C,
\]
which is not constant. Therefore there is no single numerical value under this interpretation.

\[
\boxed{\text{not uniquely determined}}
\]
